props.gloss_en: whoever makes light of the meal after bloodletting, Heaven makes light of his sustenance, and they say: he took no pity on his own life, shall I take pity on him?
one who lets blood should not sit where the wind blows
lest the bloodletter drained him and left him at a quarter[-log], and the wind come and draw from him, and he come to danger
Shmuel used to let blood in a house of seven bricks and a half [-brick thick]; one day he did so and felt [weak]; he checked, and one half-brick was missing
one who lets blood should taste something and only then go out
for if he has tasted nothing: if he meets a corpse, his face turns green; if he meets one who has killed a person, he dies
if he meets 'something else', it is harmful for 'something else'
one who lets blood should wait a little and then rise
five things are closer to death than to life: one ate and rose, drank and rose, slept and rose, let blood and rose, had relations and rose
Shmuel: the interval for bloodletting is every thirty days
and in the middle periods [of life] he should reduce, and in the [later] periods reduce again
Shmuel: the days for bloodletting are the first day of the week, the fourth, and Shabbat eve
but the second and fifth days -- not
one who has ancestral merit may let blood on the second and fifth days, for the court above and the court below are alike [on them]
the third day of the week -- why not? because Mars stands [ruling] in its even hours
Shabbat eve too stands [under Mars] in the even hours
Shmuel: a fourth [day of the week] that is the fourth [of the month], the fourteenth, the twenty-fourth, or a fourth with not four [days] after it -- danger
the New Moon and its second day -- weakness; its third -- danger
a festival eve -- weakness; the eve of Shavuot -- danger
and the Rabbis decreed on every festival eve because of [the eve of] Shavuot
for on it a wind goes out whose name is Tavoach; had Israel not accepted the Torah, it would have slaughtered their flesh and their blood
Shmuel: one who ate wheat and let blood has let blood only for that wheat
and that is for healing; but for relief, it relieves
one who lets blood: drinking -- at once
eating -- [only] after [the time to walk] half a mil
Rav announced: a hundred bloodlettings for a zuz, a hundred heads [cut] for a zuz, a hundred moustaches [trimmed] for nothing
on a day the Rabbis idled [from study], they would say: today is a day of moustaches
Rav Yosef: and I did not know what they were saying
